name: parentNode vs parentElement
description: parentNode returns the immediate parent of any node type (which could be a Document or DocumentFragment), while parentElement returns the parent only if it is itself an Element, otherwise null.
notes: parentElement is usually preferred in application code since it's guaranteed to be an Element or null.

name: children vs childNodes
description: children returns only element children (an HTMLCollection), while childNodes returns every node type including text nodes and comments (a NodeList).
notes: Use children when you only care about elements — childNodes often includes unexpected whitespace text nodes from formatting.

name: firstElementChild / lastElementChild
description: Return the first or last child that is an element, skipping over text and comment nodes.
returns: An Element, or null if there are no element children.
notes: Prefer these over firstChild/lastChild, which can return text nodes created by whitespace in the markup.

name: nextElementSibling / previousElementSibling
description: Return the next or previous sibling that is an element, skipping text and comment nodes.
returns: An Element, or null if there is no such sibling.
notes: Their non-Element counterparts (nextSibling/previousSibling) commonly return whitespace text nodes and are rarely what you want.

name: closest()
description: Walks up from an element through its ancestors (including itself) and returns the first one matching a CSS selector.
parameters: selectors — a valid CSS selector string.
returns: The matching Element, or null if no ancestor matches.
notes: The standard way to find a meaningful ancestor in an event-delegation handler.

name: contains()
description: Checks whether a node is a descendant of another node (or the same node).
returns: true if otherNode is the node itself or one of its descendants, false otherwise.
notes: A common pattern for detecting 'click outside' a component.

name: childElementCount
description: Returns the number of child elements a node has, ignoring text and comment nodes.
notes: Equivalent to but faster than element.children.length.

name: querySelector() for descendant traversal
description: Scoping querySelector()/querySelectorAll() to a specific element restricts the search to its descendants, providing flexible downward traversal beyond direct children.

name: matches()
description: Tests whether an element itself would be selected by a given CSS selector, without traversing anywhere.
parameters: selectors — a valid CSS selector string.
returns: true if the element matches, false otherwise.
notes: Frequently paired with closest() and event delegation to filter which descendant triggered an event.

name: Node.ELEMENT_NODE vs nodeType
description: Every node has a nodeType constant identifying what kind of node it is, such as 1 for elements (Node.ELEMENT_NODE) or 3 for text nodes (Node.TEXT_NODE), useful when filtering childNodes.
